messages.subject: gl.filter.secondaries doing odd things
parts:
Hi all, 

I'm not sure if this is an issue resulting from an update to dartR but the gl.filter.secondaries function doesn't seem to be working. The dataset going in has x number of loci, x number get removed, the function tells me there's x left. However, when I view the actual dataset, it tells me there's y loci left - a totally different number than was reported before, during, or even after the functino was run. 

Any ideas? I copied the whole thing below in case i'm missing something obvious. 



Cheers, 
Britt



> gl.data.filt
 /// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 270 genotypes,  5,394 binary SNPs, size: 9.2 Mb
 17782 (1.22 %) missing data

 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 270 SNPbin
   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)

 // Optional content
   @ind.names:  270 individual labels
   @loc.names:  5394 locus labels
   @loc.all:  5394 alleles
   @position: integer storing positions of the SNPs
   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 1-125)
   @other: a list containing: loc.metrics  latlong  ind.metrics  loc.metrics.flags  verbose  history 

> nosecs <- gl.filter.secondaries(gl.data.filt, method="best", v=3)
Starting gl.filter.secondaries 
  Processing a SNP dataset
  Total number of SNP loci: 5394 
  Selecting one SNP per sequence tag based on best RepAvg and AvgPIC

Completed: gl.filter.secondaries
